precepts.text: Amalek came of Eliphaz the son of Esau; the Amalekites descend from Esau.
precepts.point: The Amalekites are the seed of Esau, of Eliphaz his son. Their lineage is written in Genesis, and it is a thing to know when reading of Israel's enemies.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek”. Amalek came of Eliphaz the son of Esau, so the Amalekites are the seed of Esau.

That is who came to David from mount Gilboa. The young man said Saul asked him who he was, “And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.” He told how he found Saul leaning upon his spear with the chariots and horsemen following hard after him, and Saul said, “Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me”. So he slew him, “and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm”, and brought them to David. In the earlier account Saul fell upon his sword but did not die at that moment.

Their lineage is written in Genesis, and it is a thing to know when reading of Israel’s enemies: the Amalekite standing over Saul was of the seed of Esau.

precepts.text: Rend your heart, and not your garments; the Most High looks for true repentance within.
precepts.point: David asked the man how he was not afraid to stretch forth his hand to destroy the Lord's anointed. Even a man about to die was not to be touched; the judgment of the Lord was to be let play out. David then commanded one of his young men to fall upon the Amalekite, and he died, for his own mouth had testified against him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.”

When the news came, “David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him”, and they mourned, wept and fasted until even for Saul, for Jonathan, “and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.” The renting of garments was the sign of mourning.

But the Most High looks for a rent heart and not rent garments only. True repentance is inward, not just an outward show, and it is the heart turned unto the Lord that he is looking for.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
precepts.point: Israel's forefathers died only when the Most High said it was time; that is the only way any of them died. David mourned Jonathan, saying his love to him was wonderful, passing the love of women.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.”

David “bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow”, and his lament is “written in the book of Jasher.” The book of Jasher is not in the canon because the Most High did not will us to have it; he put in the book exactly what he wanted his people to read in the last days.

And the bow is not how this walk goes in the last days. It is not by might nor by power, but by the Spirit of the Lord. The captivity is not overthrown by rising up with the bow or the gun; this is spiritual war and not physical. There is nothing wrong with knowing how to defend yourself, but the redemption of Israel does not come by force of arms.

precepts.text: Here is the patience of the saints: they keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, not the bow or the gun.
precepts.point: Israel's forefathers died only when the Most High said it was time; that is the only way any of them died. David mourned Jonathan, saying his love to him was wonderful, passing the love of women.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” That is how Israel fights in the last days: with the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, not the bow or the gun.

David taught the children of Judah the use of the bow in his day, but the redemption of Israel does not come by force of arms. This is spiritual war and not physical, and the saints hold it with patience, keeping the commandments and the faith.

precepts.text: There is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother; so was Jonathan to David, knit at the soul.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.” So was Jonathan to David, knit at the soul.

David cried, “I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.” Jonathan was that friend closer than a brother.

The lament is a prophecy given in the spirit, almost a eulogy: “Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.” Before the devil jumped on Saul he was good, and the two of them were good together. And they died only when the Most High said it was time; that is the only way any of Israel’s forefathers died.
